english.title: Weights and measures inspector unlawfully disclose secret manufacturing process / trade secret
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[an inspector of weights and measures]_
(B)_[a person]_

who entered a workplace at **(..SPECIFY THE WORKPLACE..) by virtue of section 79 of the Weights and Measures Act 1985, disclosed to

(C)_[a person,]_
(D)_[persons,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON OR PERSONS..), information obtained by you in the workplace with regard to

(E)_[a secret manufacturing process,]_
(F)_[a trade secret,]_

the disclosure being otherwise than in the performance of your duty
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 79(7) and 84(5) of the Weights and Measures Act 1985

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 83 of the Weights and Measures Act 1985 provides: that in England and Wales, proceedings for any offence under this Act or any instrument made under this Act. shall not be instituted except by or on behalf of a local weights and measures authority or the chief officer of police for a police area.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
